status.en: 10 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 33% fewer than the week before, most of them in La Espriella, Espriella and Planadas.
status.nb: 10 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 33 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i La Espriella, Espriella og Planadas.

summary.en: Venezuela is reported to have helped a drone strike that killed two Colombian soldiers in the Choco department, while a separate bomb attack near a military base killed four civilians, including an infant. President De la Espriella has ordered a renewed military offensive against dissident groups and increased aerial spraying following the Planadas bombing. The United Nations has renewed its mission in Colombia but excluded rural reform from its mandate. The government launched a broader offensive after seven attacks in six days. The conflict recorded 225 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Venezuela skal ha bistått et droneangrep som drepte to colombianske soldater i Choco-departementet, mens et separat bombeangrep nær en militærbase drepte fire sivile, inkludert et spedbarn. President De la Espriella har beordret en fornyet militær offensiv mot dissidentgrupper og økt luftsprøyting etter Planadas-bombingen. FN har fornyet sitt oppdrag i Colombia, men har ekskludert landbruksreform fra mandatet. Regjeringen iverksatte en bredere offensiv etter syv angrep i seks dager. Konflikten registrerte 225 dødsofre i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Colombian conflict
background.extract: The Colombian conflict began on May 27, 1964, and is a low-intensity asymmetric war between the government of Colombia, paramilitary groups, crime syndicates, and far-left guerrilla groups engaged in armed factional hostilities to increase their influence in Colombian territory. Some of the most important international contributors to the Colombian conflict include multinational corporations, the United States, Cuba, and the drug trafficking industry.
